solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cameron (ex-prime minister) leaving no10 injecting American drug

parts.note: Cameron Diaz, the American film actress

indicators.note: the shortened ex-PM letters are injected with, so take inside them, the next piece
leaving says the number ten goes away from the letters before it

parts.note: read literally as EX and PM, the abbreviation for prime minister
number ten is X in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: David Cameron, having moved out of Number 10 Downing Street, starts injecting a US drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron is not the prime minister but the actress. 'leaving' removes the X (no10) from EX PM to give EPM, and 'injecting' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is a sedative medicine used against anxiety.

clue.text: Put down sample tape, having erased contents

parts.note: a demo is a sample recording

indicators.note: with its insides wiped, only the outside letters of tape are left

explanation.surface: Someone records a sample on tape, then wipes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having erased contents' leaves TE from tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce someone in rank is to put them down a grade.

clue.text: Rubbish, naff clue last in puzzle for "wealth"

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb, to trash, so the letters of naff clue are thrown about
last in picks the final letter of puzzle

explanation.surface: A grumbling solver dismisses a weak clue for wealth in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence means riches and prosperity.

clue.text: Scottish keep punishing lads butchering English

indicators.note: punishing means beating up, so the letters of lads butchering are knocked about

explanation.surface: Scots punish the lads who have been butchering the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchering' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'punishing' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a castle's stronghold; this fortress stands on a rock above the Scottish capital.

clue.text: Number-cruncher helping to deliver assurance

parts.note: a statistician working for life-assurance companies, assessing risk

explanation.surface: A calculating person helps to give reassurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Assurance reads as reassurance but is the insurance industry's term for life cover.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional calculates risks and premiums for insurers and pension funds.

clue.text: Variety of marrow pulp

definitions.meaning: a marrow is a large gourd, and this is the family of gourds it belongs to
to pulp something is to crush it flat

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a kind of marrow with soft flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a gourd such as the marrow or pumpkin; the verb means to crush to a pulp.

clue.text: Most equestrians, unfortunately, could be described as posers

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of most equestrians are jumbled

explanation.surface: Most horse riders, sadly, could be called show-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posers' looks like show-offs but means people who pose questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Quizmasters put questions, so they are posers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Humour a daughter of Mnemosyne

parts.note: the nine Muses of Greek myth were daughters of Mnemosyne and Zeus

explanation.surface: Indulge one of the daughters of the goddess of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to entertain or divert them.

clue.text: Sounds like Atwood's tale-teller is her own work!

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is spoken and a same-sounding word is entered

parts.note: Offred narrates Margaret Atwood's novel The Handmaid's Tale

explanation.surface: The narrator of Atwood's dystopian novel produced it all herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crafted personally by hand is one's own work rather than factory produced.

clue.text: Banished former partner (idle drunk)

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters of idle stagger about

explanation.surface: An idle, drunken ex was sent packing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be driven out of one's country is to be banished.

clue.text: Learned Muslim character from Greece heads two newspapers

indicators.note: heads means the Greek letter goes at the front of what follows

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the FT (Financial Times) and the i, two British newspapers

explanation.surface: A Greek man is in charge of two newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national daily paper; FT is the Financial Times, the paper that publishes this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is an Islamic scholar who gives rulings on religious law.

clue.text: Financial statement using extra spin

indicators.note: using in the sense of exploiting or working over, so the letters of extra are rearranged

parts.note: a spin is a turn, as a spin around the block

explanation.surface: Someone puts an extra bit of positive spin on their accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is a rare anagram signal: the letters of EXTRA are worked over into TAXRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The form filed annually with tax authorities is a statement of one's income and finances.

clue.text: Sample of photo is a handy feature

definitions.meaning: a small preview version of a picture
punning on hand: something found on the hand, at the tip of the digit

explanation.surface: A small preview of a picture is described as a useful thing to have.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature preview image takes its name from the hard plate on the end of a person's first digit.

clue.text: The Marines unit displaying heat

parts.note: the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry corps, are abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A military unit of marines shows signs of getting hot.
explanation.walkthrough: As shown, the clue has lost its opening 'The', which the parse needs. 'unit' looks military but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a measure of heat energy, used in billing for gas.

clue.text: Where work is to be done within year?

definitions.text: Where work is to be done

parts.note: intra is the Latin prefix meaning within

explanation.surface: A question about where work gets done in the course of a year.
explanation.walkthrough: INTRA- is the prefix meaning within, as in intravenous.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tray holds papers waiting to be dealt with, the pile of jobs still to do.

clue.text: Left out retiring actor Johnny, old, raddled, discontented

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Johnny Depp, the American film actor

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the outside letters of raddled remain

explanation.surface: A worn-out old actor called Johnny is being dropped from a production as he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' leaves RD from raddled; DEPP + O + RD then runs backwards under 'retiring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dropped from a team has been omitted from it.

clue.text: Catastrophe! No men allowed to host these amazing events

indicators.note: to host means the phrase contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Disaster: a men-only ban for some remarkable occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catastrophe!' looks like an exclamation, but its last letters start the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels.

clue.text: Cor! 10CC's new stream is hot!

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
10CC, the British rock band, with 10 read as the letters I and O, plus the S

explanation.surface: An excited fan exclaims that the band 10cc's new stream is hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT printed 'A!' where the setter wrote 'Cor!'; the anagram only works with COR. 'new' reshuffles COR with I, O, C, C and S.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa is a stream of air.

clue.text: Oh heck! Poor Victor … he died of TB

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters of oh heck are reformed

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An exclamation of sympathy for a poor man called Victor who died of tuberculosis.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like the man's name; it is the radio code word for V.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov, the Russian playwright, died of tuberculosis in 1904.

clue.text: Upturned box containing a tin (empty)

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
in a down clue upturned means written bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the box is slang for a television, TV
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An upside-down box with a tin in it is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is the container signal; 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or with nothing inside.

clue.text: Cranking up REM following intro from Jerry Springer

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the initial
the intro of a word is its opening letter
cranking means twisting round, so the letters of up and REM are churned

explanation.surface: Turning up the band REM's music after the start of the Jerry Springer show.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry Springer looks like one name; 'Jerry' gives J and 'Springer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who leaps is one who springs.

clue.text: Ms Adamson holding lion's ear regularly, such skilful handiwork!

indicators.note: holding means the name wraps around the letters that follow

parts.note: Joy Adamson, who raised the lioness Elsa in Born Free

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of lion's ear

explanation.surface: Joy Adamson, of Born Free fame, holds a lion by the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I, N, E, R from lion's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Joinery is the craft of carpentry, skilled woodwork made by hand.

clue.text: One of three notes beginning to explain Earth's natural attraction?

parts.note: one of three notes could be G, F or C, written as letters G F OR C

indicators.note: the beginning of explain is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical teacher uses notes to start explaining gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of three notes' is read as the phrase 'G, F or C'. The question mark admits the definition is loose: the term measures acceleration, not only Earth's pull.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit is defined by the pull of gravity at the Earth's surface.

clue.text: Measure, say, Reading University business grad

parts.note: R, from the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A business graduate of Reading University is asked to measure something.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town with a university, but here it gives R. 'Measure' is an old word for a stately dance; 'say' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance is an example of a measure in its older sense of a dance.

clue.text: Minister's house servant cleaning out staircase

parts.note: a man is a manservant

indicators.note: cleaning out empties the middle, leaving only the outside letters of staircase

explanation.surface: A servant cleans the staircase at the minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a Scottish or Presbyterian clergyman's residence.

clue.text: Crow flies around, winds people up

indicators.note: around means moved about, so the letters of crow flies are shuffled

explanation.surface: A crow flies in circles, annoying people.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising false alarms, as the boy in Aesop's fable did, alarms and teases others.

clue.text: Lady Chatterley's right-wing position

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the right-wing British party
a stance is a position or standpoint

explanation.surface: Lady Chatterley holds right-wing views.
explanation.definitionFit: In D H Lawrence's novel the title character's first name is Constance.

clue.text: HM receiving Julius, eastern ruler

indicators.note: receiving means the royal letters take in the setter and the E, which go ahead of them

parts.note: Julius is the setter, who refers to himself as me
Her Majesty, the Queen, is ER

explanation.surface: Her Majesty welcomes Julius, an eastern potentate.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is Julius, so the name gives ME. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir, here in an older spelling, is a prince or governor in the Muslim world.

clue.text: Specialist batsman no stranger to the bottle?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, one of the two batsmen who start an innings
punning on a drinker's familiarity with bottles: the tool that uncaps them

explanation.surface: A cricketer is known to like a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it is the first-order batter; in a kitchen it is the gadget for removing caps.

clue.text: British passport used to feature this cover

definitions.text: British passport used to feature this
definitions.meaning: old British passports recorded the colour of the holder's eyes
a visor shielding the face from glare

explanation.surface: An old British passport carried a picture of this sort of cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Old passports listed the holder's eye colour, read here as two words, 'eye shade'.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor worn on the forehead keeps glare off the face.
